name: POST /api/sla/clocks/merge - Fold a merged-away subject into the survivor
skipReason: Needs TWO INDEPENDENTLY CREATED clocks. The create->capture chain in this suite yields exactly one clock_id, so an automated case could only merge a clock into itself - which is not the behaviour worth pinning and would leave the survivor pointing at its own cancellation. Covered by packages/sdk-sla/tests/clock.integration.test.ts, which creates both clocks directly. This is a TWO-PRODUCER limitation of one-definition-per-METHOD+ENDPOINT, not a missing payload or an uncaptured path param - it is not the case MUST-49 forbids marking manual.
description: When two subjects turn out to be one, fold the absorbed clock into the survivor. The survivor keeps ITS OWN timing — the promise the platform made first is the one it owes — and records merged_from_ref so it still names what it absorbed; the absorbed clock is cancelled with a pointer to the survivor so the trail stays intact. Neither clock's source_timestamp, started_at or due_at moves, and a database trigger enforces that: a merge is one of the moments a system is most tempted to "refresh" a clock, which would erase a wait somebody has already had. Returns 200 with both clocks. MANUAL: needs TWO independently created clocks and the create->capture chain yields one clock_id, so an automated case would have to merge a clock into itself. Covered by packages/sdk-sla/tests/clock.integration.test.ts. Required: tenant_id, surviving_clock_id, merged_clock_id.

statusTransitions.note: at_risk is a DERIVED view over running/paused clocks approaching due_at (GET /api/sla/at-risk), not a stored state — the column can only hold the five values in fieldEnums.state.

transitions.note: a missed promise can still be kept, late — satisfied_at then sits after due_at so attainment still counts it as a miss
